title: Blessed State! and Happy He
description: Blessed State! and Happy He in Tonic Solfa to VIENNA, doh is G: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Bernard Barton wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 964 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “"He shall be like a tree planted in the rivers of water."”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens (7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to VIENNA; any other Sevens tune fits them as well.
underlay: Bless-ed state! and hap-py he Who is like that plant-ed tree; Liv-ing wa-ters lave his root, Bends his bough with gol-den fruit.

lines: Who is like that planted tree;
Bends his bough with golden fruit.
When the seedling from its bed
First lifts up its timid head,
All on which its life can live.
Showers from thee must bid it thrive,
Breath of thine must oft revive;
Light from thee its bloom supplies, —
Left by thee it fades and dies.
Thine, O Lord! the power and praise
Which a sight like this displays;
Power of thine must plant it there,
Praise of thee it should declare.

licence: Public domain: Bernard Barton died in 1849.
credits: Words by Bernard Barton (1784–1849), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to VIENNA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
